text: [BLOCKER] The "3D structure" is a parametric ASCII-driven helix, not a protein backbone; geometry is wrong by scale-free measures — The renderer produces no protein geometry of any kind. Each "residue" position is sin/cos of an index times a radius derived from the residue's ASCII code modulo 5 — a cyclic function of the alphabet, not of chemistry. Three independent, scale-free tests fail. (1) Virtual bond length: re-running app.js:711-729 in Python on the actual sequences gives consecutive point separations of 1.91-19.08 units (drug X1, L=47), 0.63-16.63 (X3), 2.14-16.22 (P1); coefficient of variation 0.56-0.82 and max/min ratios of 8-26x. Real Cα-Cα virtual bond length is 3.80-3.81 Å with sigma ~0.04 Å (CV ~1%), fixed by the planar trans peptide bond (omega ~180°); it does not vary with residue identity. Because CV and max/min are invariant to any unit scaling, no choice of Å-per-scene-unit rescues this. (2) The cause of the scatter is that `angle` at app.js:717 is recomputed from scratch at each i with a multiplier that flips between 4 and 6 depending on that residue's ASCII code mod 3 (E,H,K,N,Q,T,W,B,Z take 6; everything else 4). The angle is therefore non-monotonic — verified on X1: i=5(N) angle=2.005 rad, i=6(P) angle=1.604 rad. The chain jumps backwards and across the cylinder, producing the 19-unit "bonds". (3) Helical parameters: rise per residue is a constant 0.6 units (app.js:716) and radius is 6.0-9.2 units (11.96 with the C/P ×1.3 factor), giving radius/rise = 10.0-19.9. For an alpha-helix that ratio is 2.3/1.5 = 1.53 — the model is off by 6.5-13x, again scale-free. Residues per turn is L/2 or L/3, i.e. 13-24 for these designs (50 for the 100-mer at app.js:125) versus 3.6 for alpha-helix, 3.0 for 3-10, 4.4 for pi, and ~2 for beta-strand; the model's helical period scales with chain length, which is physically meaningless. Finally, the covalently attached natural-product warhead — the defining feature of a "bio-conjugate" — is never represented by a single atom, and the target receptor (TrkB, AChE, Keap1, ...) is never rendered, so no binding pose exists anywhere in the codebase despite ΔG and Kd being quoted for every entry. Consequence: The image on screen is the platform's primary evidence that these 25 molecules were structurally modelled. A reader — a collaborator, a reviewer, an investor, an IRB — sees a ribbon with pLDDT-coloured residue spheres and reasonably concludes a structure prediction was run and inspected. It was not. Any downstream decision that depends on the fold, the presentation of the warhead, the accessibility of the binding epitope, or the compatibility of the peptide with its stated receptor pocket is being made against a decorative sine wave. Because the comment at app.js:707 and the README explicitly assert the parsing is "real", this is an affirmative misrepresentation rather than an acknowledged placeholder.

text: Ground truth for SB-01: Protein backbone geometry is determined by covalent restraints (Engh & Huber 1991) plus the phi/psi torsions; Cα(i)-Cα(i+1) = 3.80 Å for trans peptides (~2.9 Å for the rare cis-Pro). Alpha-helix: 3.6 residues/turn, 1.5 Å rise/residue, 5.4 Å pitch, ~2.3 Å Cα radius, phi/psi ≈ (-57°, -47°), stabilised by i→i+4 N-H···O=C hydrogen bonds. Beta-strand: ~3.3-3.4 Å rise, phi/psi ≈ (-120°, +130°). Secondary structure is assigned from backbone H-bonding and geometry (DSSP), never from residue identity — the same residue adopts helix, strand or coil depending on context, which is precisely why sequence-to-structure is a hard prediction problem rather than a lookup. A structure of a covalent bio-conjugate must contain the warhead atoms and, to support any ΔG claim, the receptor.

text: [BLOCKER] pLDDT profiles and PAE heatmaps are closed-form functions of ASCII codes and residue index, containing zero information from any predictor — pLDDT is generated as 93 + 4·sin(0.4i) + 0.5·(ASCII mod 5). Its range over every possible input is [89.0, 99.0] (computed: min 93-4+0, max 93+4+2), so the clamps at app.js:792-793 (>100→98.6, <70→76) are unreachable dead code and no residue can ever fall below 89. The UI legend at index.html:390-391 advertises "Low (50-70)" and "Very Low (<50)" bands that the generator cannot produce. The sin term has period 2π/0.4 = 15.71 residues, so every one of the 25 molecules displays the same waveform with a ±1.0 ASCII ripple — verified means: X1 93.92, X3 94.30, P1 94.29. PAE is 0.4·|i-j| plus a row-constant ASCII offset: it is a pure function of sequence separation, so it can never show the off-diagonal low-error blocks that are the entire diagnostic content of a PAE matrix (rigid inter-domain packing, well-defined interfaces). Its maximum attainable value on a 45×45 grid is 44·0.4+0.9 = 18.5 Å, yet the panel title claims a 0-30 Å scale. Separately, the residue spheres at app.js:747-749 are coloured by amino-acid letter — G/S mapped to the "High" band, P/D to the "Low" band — which asserts that residue identity determines local confidence. Consequence: pLDDT and PAE are the only quantities that tell a structural biologist which parts of a prediction may be trusted. Presenting synthetic curves under the label "AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score" inverts their function: every candidate is rendered as uniformly "Very High" confidence, which is exactly the signal a reader uses to decide the model is good enough to design experiments against. A flat 89-99 band with no low-confidence regions is also intrinsically implausible for short, Cys-rich, linker-containing designed peptides, which in practice show pLDDT collapsing to 30-60 across GGGGS linkers and termini. The colour rule is affirmatively wrong science: Gly and Pro are the two residues most associated with backbone flexibility and *low* local confidence, and Ser and Asp are unremarkable — the mapping is not merely arbitrary, it is close to inverted for Gly.

text: Ground truth for SB-02: pLDDT is the network's per-atom/per-residue estimate of the lDDT-Cα score (Mariani et al. 2013) — a prediction about that specific model's local accuracy, emitted by the confidence head and written to the B-factor column of the output mmCIF and to the accompanying confidences JSON. It is a property of the model, conditioned on the full input (sequence, MSA, ligands, stoichiometry), not of the amino-acid alphabet. PAE(i,j) is the expected positional error at residue j when the prediction and true structure are aligned on residue i; it is genuinely asymmetric, is emitted as a full N×N matrix (AF3 caps at 31.75 Å), and its block structure is what identifies domains and confident interfaces. The AF3 paper explicitly warns that geometry is rendered sharply regardless of confidence: "the local structure will be sharply defined (for example, side-chain bond geometry) even when the network is uncertain about the positions" — which is why the confidence arrays, not the rendered geometry, must be the source of colouring.

text: [BLOCKER] AlphaFold 3 cannot model a covalently conjugated natural-product warhead in the way claimed, and no prediction was ever submitted — Every one of the 25 entities is described as a small-molecule warhead covalently coupled to a peptide, i.e. exactly the case AF3 handles least freely. Three concrete gaps. (1) The public AlphaFold Server accepts ligands only from a fixed allow-list (CCD_ATP, ADP, AMP, GTP, GDP, FAD, NAD, NAP, NDP, HEM, HEC, PLM, OLA, MYR, CIT, CLA, CHL, BCL, BCB, plus ten common ions); arbitrary SMILES are rejected. None of ginsenoside Rg1/Rb1/Rg3, huperzine A, curcumin, asiatic acid, salvianolic acid B, ginkgolide B, bilobalide, ferulic acid or presenegenin is on that list, so not one of these conjugates can be submitted to the Server at all — and the only "integration" in the code is an anchor tag plus a clipboard copy of the bare peptide, which would model the peptide alone with the pharmacophore silently discarded. (2) The local AF3 code does accept SMILES, but its own documentation states: "If using SMILES, you cannot specify covalent bonds to other entities as these rely on specific atom names", and "Defining covalent bonds between or within polymer entities is not currently supported." A covalent conjugate therefore requires the author to write a full user-supplied CCD block (named atoms, bond orders, charges, leaving atoms, ideal coordinates) and an explicit bondedAtomPairs entry — non-trivial cheminformatics work that appears nowhere in this repository. (3) Input hygiene: the sequences at app.js:173 and app.js:371 contain 'B' (Asx, an ambiguity code, not an amino acid) and would be rejected by both the Server and the local parser. A related instance of unmodelled chemistry: drug #9 (app.js:225) is exactly GSK-3β residues 3-34 (verified against UniProt P49841, MSGRPRTTSFAESCKPVQQPSAFGSMKVSRDKDG...), a genuinely sensible pseudosubstrate choice — but it only inhibits when Ser9 is phosphorylated, and no phosphoserine (CCD SEP) modification is specified anywhere. Finally, AF3 emits no free energy: there is no scoring function in AF3 that produces kcal/mol, so the ΔG and Kd values throughout cannot have come from the tool credited with producing them. Consequence: The central claim of the platform — 25 therapeutics "designed via AlphaFold3" — is not achievable with the described inputs and was demonstrably not attempted. A structural biologist or medicinal chemist reading the README will assume the conjugation geometry was modelled: whether the linker reaches, whether the warhead is presented toward the pocket, whether conjugation occludes the binding epitope. Those are the questions a bio-conjugate design lives or dies on, and none of them can even be posed without bondedAtomPairs plus a userCCD. Anyone attempting to reproduce this work would discover at the first submission that the Server refuses the ligand and the sequence, and would conclude the results were never generated.

text: Required fix for SB-03: Either (a) actually run local AF3 with, for each conjugate, a userCCD block defining the warhead (atom names, bonds, charges, leaving atoms, ideal geometry generated with RDKit or the CCD tooling), a bondedAtomPairs entry defining the conjugation bond to the named side-chain atom of the correct residue, the receptor as a second protein entity so a pose exists, and explicit SEP/other CCD modification codes where the mechanism requires them — then commit the resulting mmCIF and confidences JSON; or (b) drop "AlphaFold3" from every claim and relabel the entries as unmodelled design concepts. Fix the invalid 'B' residues at app.js:173 and app.js:371. Separately, replace all ΔG/Kd values with either output from a tool that actually computes them (FEP/MM-GBSA/docking, with the method and settings stated) or with nothing.

tags: Structural biology — macromolecular structure determination and validation (X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM), structure-prediction model assessment, and molecular graphics
text: Ground truth for SB-03: AlphaFold 3 (Abramson et al., Nature 630:493-500, 2024) predicts joint structures of proteins, nucleic acids, ligands, ions and modified residues. Local code: ligands via CCD code, SMILES, or user-provided CCD; covalent linkage only via bondedAtomPairs, which requires named atoms and therefore a CCD/userCCD entity, not a SMILES; no covalent bonds within or between polymer entities. AlphaFold Server: restricted ligand/ion allow-list, restricted PTM list, no arbitrary SMILES, no user CCD. AF3 also has documented physical failure modes relevant here — "the model outputs do not always respect chirality" (4.4% chirality violations on the PoseBusters set), "a tendency of the model to occasionally produce overlapping (clashing) atoms", and "spurious structural order (hallucinations) in disordered regions" — all of which apply with force to short designed peptides. AF3 predicts a single static conformation, not an ensemble, and outputs no binding free energy.

text: [CRITICAL] Four pairs of candidates share byte-identical sequences yet report different pLDDT and ΔG — Programmatic extraction of all 25 entries shows four sequences each used twice, under different candidate codes, assigned to different brain regions and different receptors (e.g. the same 41-mer is both an α7 nAChR ECD binder, PfcACh-PAM-P1, and a TLR4/MD-2 antagonist, MicroTlr4-Antagonist-M3), with different reported pLDDT and different reported ΔG. pLDDT is a deterministic function of the model input; for the same sequence with the same conditioning it is identical, and even across seeds it would not drift in a way that correlates with which marketing label the entry carries. The application's own renderer demonstrates the contradiction: because both the 3D geometry (app.js:711-729) and the pLDDT curve (app.js:791) are pure functions of the sequence string, opening the two modals produces pixel-identical structures and identical confidence curves while the summary panel beside them displays different numbers. Consequence: Identical input with divergent reported output is a positive signature that the numbers were written by hand rather than read from a computation. It also means the ranking of the 25 candidates — the leaderboard, the ΔG bar chart at app.js:1049-1102, the 'Peak Binding Energy -19.5 kcal' hero stat at index.html:74 — is ordered on invented quantities. Any reader who takes this table as a prioritisation for synthesis would be allocating wet-lab resources on the basis of numbers with no generating process.

AF3's confidence head produces one pLDDT array per predicted sample; the same sequence conditioned the same way yields the same array. None of that structure exists here; the two entries share one bare peptide string and no receptor entity.

text: [CRITICAL] 103 cysteines across 25 designs, 11 with an odd count, with no disulfide connectivity specified anywhere — and one conjugation chemistry that requires a cysteine the sequence does not contain — Cysteine-rich designs are specified purely as one-letter strings with no disulfide topology. Eight cysteines admit 105 distinct fully-paired connectivities (7!! = 105); six admit 15; four admit 3 — and each is a different molecule with a different fold, not a different conformer of one molecule. Eleven of the designs have an odd cysteine count and therefore cannot be fully paired at all: at least one free thiol remains, which under oxidising extracellular or serum conditions drives disulfide scrambling, intermolecular dimerisation, and mixed disulfides with albumin Cys34 and glutathione. This is not a modelling nicety for these particular targets: the peptides are explicitly presented as CRD/Ig-domain and knottin-like binders (FZD8 CRD at app.js:174, TrkB Ig-like D5 at app.js:144), folds whose entire specificity derives from a defined cystine framework. Separately, app.js:152 states the huperzine A warhead is attached by "Cys-Lys Amide Coupling" to a 36-mer (app.js:153) containing no cysteine — the stated conjugation chemistry has no anchor in the stated sequence. Consequence: Without a specified cystine framework these are not defined chemical entities, and any predicted structure is a prediction about an arbitrary one of up to 105 possible molecules. In practice, a synthesis attempt on a 7- or 8-Cys peptide with unspecified pairing yields a heterogeneous mixture of oxidised isomers that cannot be resolved into the intended product; the odd-Cys designs additionally aggregate. Reporting a single pLDDT and a single Kd for such an entity implies a homogeneity that cannot exist, and would send a peptide-chemistry group down a months-long dead end. The X2 contradiction is worse in kind: the conjugation step described cannot be performed on the molecule described.

text: Required fix for SB-05: For every Cys-containing design, publish the intended disulfide connectivity explicitly (e.g. C1-C4, C2-C5, C3-C6) and the intended redox state of any deliberately free thiol. Make Cys count parity a hard validation rule: no design ships with an odd count unless the free thiol is the deliberate conjugation handle and is named as such. Verify the pairing in each predicted mmCIF by measuring Sγ-Sγ distances and χ3 angles and reporting them; flag any pair outside 2.0-2.1 Å / ±(75-105)°. Reconcile every chemStruct conjugation chemistry against the sequence — starting with app.js:152/153, where either a Cys must be introduced or the coupling chemistry restated. Choose orthogonal protection consistent with the declared pairing before any synthesis is proposed.

tags: Structural biology — macromolecular structure determination and validation (X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM), structure-prediction model assessment, and molecular graphics
text: Ground truth for SB-05: A disulfide is a covalent bond with tight geometry — Sγ-Sγ ≈ 2.05 Å, Cβ-Sγ-Sγ ≈ 104°, χ3 (Cβ-Sγ-Sγ-Cβ) ≈ ±87° with a strong left-handed-spiral preference — and validation packages (MolProbity, wwPDB OneDep) flag deviations, non-bonded Cys pairs within bonding distance, and unpaired buried thiols. Cystine-stabilised scaffolds (knottins, EGF/Ig folds, Wnt/FZD CRD interfaces) are defined by their connectivity pattern, which must be stated as part of the sequence definition. In AF3, standard CYS residues can form disulfides implicitly, but the pairing is not user-controllable from a bare sequence and must be verified in the output; deliberate control requires explicit chemistry. In synthesis, defined pairing requires orthogonal protecting-group strategies (Trt/Acm/Mob/tBu) and staged oxidation, and the number of Cys must be even.

text: [MAJOR] No structure validation of any kind exists — no MolProbity/Ramachandran, no clashscore, no bond-geometry check, no PoseBusters ligand-pose check — The platform presents itself as structural pharmacology output but contains no validation layer whatsoever — and cannot have one, since no coordinate file is ever produced or read. Absent are: backbone torsion validation (Ramachandran favoured/allowed/outlier percentages, Cβ deviations), all-atom steric validation (clashscore from reduced/probe-style H-atom contact analysis), covalent-geometry validation (bond-length and bond-angle Z-scores against Engh & Huber targets, peptide omega/planarity, cis-nonPro and twisted-peptide flags, chirality at Cα), rotamer outliers, and — most important for a ligand-conjugate platform — any physical-plausibility check on the ligand and its pose (internal energy, ring planarity, stereochemistry retention, protein-ligand steric overlap, ligand-in-pocket volume). Disulfide geometry validation is likewise absent (see SB-05). Consequence: These checks are the reason the field trusts any set of coordinates; they are mandatory in wwPDB deposition and are the first thing a reviewer runs on a predicted model. Their absence means nothing in this platform distinguishes a physically realisable molecule from one with inverted stereocentres, clashing atoms, or a warhead buried inside the peptide. This matters concretely for AF3 output specifically, because the AF3 authors report that their model "outputs do not always respect chirality" (4.4% chirality violations on the PoseBusters benchmark) and shows "a tendency ... to occasionally produce overlapping (clashing) atoms" — i.e. the very failure modes that only validation catches are known to occur at non-trivial rates in the tool being credited. Publishing predicted conjugate poses without PoseBusters-class checks is, since 2024, below the accepted standard of the field.

tags: Structural biology — macromolecular structure determination and validation (X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM), structure-prediction model assessment, and molecular graphics
text: Required fix for SB-06: Add a validation stage that runs on every predicted mmCIF before any result is displayed: (1) MolProbity (or the phenix.molprobity CLI) for clashscore, Ramachandran favoured/outlier %, rotamer outliers, Cβ deviations, and cis/twisted peptides; (2) PoseBusters on every ligand pose in the conjugate and, where a receptor is modelled, on the protein-ligand pair; (3) explicit disulfide geometry measurement per SB-05; (4) a bond-length/angle Z-score summary against Engh & Huber. Surface these numbers in the UI next to pLDDT — a real validation panel is the honest replacement for the current confidence theatre — and gate publication on thresholds (e.g. clashscore < 10, Ramachandran outliers < 0.5%, zero PoseBusters failures), with any candidate that fails marked as such rather than hidden.

tags: Structural biology — macromolecular structure determination and validation (X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM), structure-prediction model assessment, and molecular graphics
text: Ground truth for SB-06: MolProbity (Williams et al., Protein Science 27:293-315, 2018) is the community standard for all-atom validation and supplies clashscore, updated Ramachandran and rotamer criteria from a million quality-filtered residues, CaBLAM for low-resolution/cryo-EM backbone, and cis-nonPro/twisted-peptide flags; its clashscore is the metric the wwPDB tracks. wwPDB validation reports (Gore et al., Structure 25:1916-1927, 2017) codify the required checks for deposition. Engh & Huber (Acta Cryst A47:392-400, 1991) provide the target bond lengths and angles. PoseBusters (Buttenschoen, Morris & Deane, Chem. Sci. 15:3130-3139, 2024) is the standard physical-validity test suite for ligand poses — chemical validity, stereochemistry, internal geometry, and intra/intermolecular plausibility including protein-ligand clashes — and established that pose RMSD alone is not sufficient evidence of a usable prediction.

text: [MAJOR] Renderer accepts and silently visualises non-sequence input; residue markers are index-shifted, half-sampled, and the 'binding site' is a fixed sphere at the origin — Four defects, each independently visible. (1) Drug #24's sequence field is not a sequence but the prose string "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate". It is nonetheless fed to all three visualisers: verified output shows a 37-'residue' model whose pLDDT chart is labelled H1, i2, s3, 14, 45, -6, P7, h8 — digits, hyphens and lowercase letters rendered as amino acids with confidence scores (e.g. '14' → 99.0). It is also what copyModalFasta() (app.js:660-671) puts on the clipboard under a button offering to submit it to AlphaFold Server. (2) THREE.CatmullRomCurve3.getPoint(t) maps t to control-point index (N-1)·t, so getPoint(i/seqLength) returns the position of index i·(L-1)/L, not i — every residue marker is displaced by i/L control points, approaching a full residue at the C-terminus, so markers are coloured by one residue's identity while sitting at another's position. (3) The loop steps i += 2, so only half the residues get a marker at all, while the legend at index.html:387-392 implies a complete per-residue colouring. (4) The green wireframe sphere labelled 'bindingSite' is a constant-radius sphere hardcoded at (0,0,0) in both viewers, with no relation to any pocket, epitope, or the bindingSites strings shown in the same modal. Consequence: Defect (1) proves the pipeline has no input validation and that no human ever inspected the output for all 25 entries — a prose string produced a confident-looking 3D model, a 92.4 pLDDT, and a PAE heatmap without any error. It also means a user who clicks 'Copy FASTA Sequence' and 'Launch AlphaFold Server' on that card pastes garbage into the Server. Defects (2) and (3) mean that even under the platform's own (invalid) colouring rule, the coloured markers do not correspond to the residues they claim to. Defect (4) presents an arbitrary sphere as a binding site, which a reader will interpret as a computed pocket. Together these show the visualisation was never checked against its own inputs.

text: Ground truth for SB-07: Any sequence-consuming pipeline must validate against the 20 standard one-letter codes plus explicitly permitted modification codes, and reject ambiguity codes (B = Asx, Z = Glx, X, J) — both the AlphaFold Server and the local AF3 parser do exactly this. Residue-indexed annotations must be keyed to the residue index in the coordinate file (label_seq_id / auth_seq_id in mmCIF), never to an arc-length or normalised curve parameter. Binding sites in a real viewer are defined by the coordinates of the pocket residues in the predicted complex — selected by residue number and rendered as surface or contact representation — not by a placeholder primitive.

tags: Structural biology — macromolecular structure determination and validation (X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM), structure-prediction model assessment, and molecular graphics
text: Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3 (2024). The AF3 model itself, plus the authors' own limitations: chirality is not always respected (4.4% violations on the PoseBusters set), occasional overlapping/clashing atoms including whole-chain overlaps in homomers, hallucinated order in disordered regions mitigated by AF2 cross-distillation, prediction of a single static structure rather than solution dynamics, and the warning that 'the local structure will be sharply defined (for example, side-chain bond geometry) even when the network is uncertain about the positions'. Application here: Establishes the ground truth for SB-03 (what AF3 is and outputs — notably no ΔG) and supplies the field's own justification for SB-06: the failure modes AF3 is documented to exhibit are precisely the ones that only post-hoc validation detects, so publishing predicted conjugate poses without validation is below standard.

tags: Structural biology — macromolecular structure determination and validation (X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM), structure-prediction model assessment, and molecular graphics
text: AlphaFold 3 input documentation (google-deepmind/alphafold3, docs/input.md) (2025). The authoritative input contract: ligands by CCD code, SMILES, or user-provided CCD; bondedAtomPairs 'intended for modelling covalent ligands, and for defining multi-CCD ligands (e.g. glycans)'; and the two decisive restrictions — 'If using SMILES, you cannot specify covalent bonds to other entities as these rely on specific atom names' and 'Defining covalent bonds between or within polymer entities is not currently supported.' Application here: Directly grounds SB-03: a covalent natural-product-to-peptide conjugate cannot be specified by SMILES alone; it requires a userCCD block with named atoms plus an explicit bondedAtomPairs entry, neither of which exists in this repository.

tags: Structural biology — macromolecular structure determination and validation (X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM), structure-prediction model assessment, and molecular graphics
text: PoseBusters: AI-based docking methods fail to generate physically valid poses or generalise to novel sequences (2024). An RDKit-based test suite for the physical validity of ligand poses — chemical and geometric consistency including stereochemistry, aromatic-ring planarity, standard bond lengths, and intra/intermolecular plausibility including protein-ligand clashes — and the finding that no deep-learning docking method beats classical docking once physical plausibility is scored alongside RMSD. Application here: This is the missing check named in SB-06. Every conjugate pose (warhead + linker + peptide, and the receptor complex if predicted) must pass PoseBusters before any pose-derived claim is displayed; PoseBusters is also the benchmark on which AF3's 4.4% chirality-violation rate was measured.

tags: Structural biology — macromolecular structure determination and validation (X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM), structure-prediction model assessment, and molecular graphics
text: MolProbity: More and better reference data for improved all-atom structure validation (2018). The community-standard all-atom validation suite: clashscore from explicit-H contact analysis, Ramachandran and rotamer criteria rebuilt from a million quality-filtered residues, CaBLAM Cα-CO virtual-angle analysis for low-resolution and cryo-EM backbone, and flags for rare cis-nonPro and twisted peptides. Application here: Defines the exact validation stage absent per SB-06. Run MolProbity on every predicted mmCIF and surface clashscore, Ramachandran favoured/outlier %, rotamer outliers and Cβ deviations in the UI in place of the synthetic pLDDT panel.

tags: Structural biology — macromolecular structure determination and validation (X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM), structure-prediction model assessment, and molecular graphics
text: Validation of Structures in the Protein Data Bank (2017). The wwPDB OneDep validation framework and the expert-task-force recommendations behind the standard validation report for X-ray, NMR and cryo-EM structures. Application here: Provides the deposition-grade checklist a platform claiming 'structural pharmacology' should be measured against, and the template for the validation panel recommended in SB-06.

tags: Structural biology — macromolecular structure determination and validation (X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM), structure-prediction model assessment, and molecular graphics
text: lDDT: a local superposition-free score for comparing protein structures and models using distance difference tests (2013). The definition of the local Distance Difference Test — the quantity that pLDDT predicts — including its superposition-free construction and its stereochemical-plausibility component. Application here: Grounds SB-02: pLDDT is a per-residue estimate of lDDT-Cα for a specific predicted model, read from the mmCIF B-factor column or the confidences JSON. It is not a function of the amino-acid alphabet, which is what app.js:791 and the G/S/P/D colour rule at app.js:747-749 assume.

tags: Structural biology — macromolecular structure determination and validation (X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM), structure-prediction model assessment, and molecular graphics
text: Mol* Viewer: modern web app for 3D visualization and analysis of large biomolecular structures (2021). The web-native molecular viewer used as the primary 3D viewer by both RCSB PDB and PDBe; streams and renders mmCIF/BinaryCIF, supports per-atom colouring from B-factor (hence pLDDT), ligand and polymer representations, and selection-based highlighting. Application here: The recommended replacement for the synthetic Three.js tube in SB-01: load the predicted mmCIF, colour by the real pLDDT array, and render warhead and receptor so an actual binding pose is shown.

tags: Structural biology — macromolecular structure determination and validation (X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM), structure-prediction model assessment, and molecular graphics
text: 3Dmol.js: molecular visualization with WebGL (2015). A lightweight, dependency-free JavaScript/WebGL molecular viewer with hardware-accelerated cartoon, stick and surface representations and PDB/mmCIF parsing, requiring no plugins. Application here: A drop-in alternative to Mol* for this vanilla-JS, CDN-only codebase — it fits the existing architecture almost exactly and would replace app.js:674-773 and app.js:959-1022 with a real structure viewer at comparable code size.

tags: Structural biology — macromolecular structure determination and validation (X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM), structure-prediction model assessment, and molecular graphics
text: Accurate bond and angle parameters for X-ray protein structure refinement (1991). The standard restraint targets for protein covalent geometry — bond lengths and angles derived from small-molecule crystal structures in the CSD, with force constants reflecting observed variability. Application here: The reference against which the geometry in SB-01 fails and against which the bond-geometry Z-scores recommended in SB-06 should be computed. It is the basis for the fixed 3.80 Å Cα-Cα virtual bond length that the app.js:711-729 generator violates by up to 26-fold within a single chain.
